name: Brendan Eich
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Created JavaScript at Netscape in 1995 at age 33–34; earlier SGI systems work and 1985 MS from Illinois were ordinary early-career steps, not independently breakout achievements.
early_history_summary: Born July 4, 1961 in Pittsburgh; raised partly in Maryland and Palo Alto. Earned BS in math/CS at Santa Clara and MS (1985) from University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, then spent ~7 years at Silicon Graphics on OS and network code before joining Netscape in April 1995.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond places of upbringing.
evidence_summary: Eich’s defining achievement—inventing JavaScript in ten days at Netscape in 1995—occurred at age 33–34. Pre-26 record is standard CS training plus SGI engineering employment without a dated public breakout product, language, or company. Family and early-advantage detail is sparse in public sources.

name: Henrique Dubugras
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Brazilian payments company Pagar.me in 2013 at about age 17–18; grew it to ~100–150 employees and ~$1.5B GMV, then sold it to StoneCo in 2016 at age ~21; co-founded Brex in January 2017 at age ~21–22 via Y Combinator.
early_history_summary: Born 1995 in São Paulo, Brazil; started coding ~age 12 (games). Met co-founder Pedro Franceschi via a Twitter argument while still in high school; together built Pagar.me as a Stripe-like processor for Brazil, won Microsoft Startup of the Year (2014), sold in 2016, briefly enrolled at Stanford CS, then dropped out to found Brex.
family_context_summary: Raised in São Paulo, Brazil; public profiles emphasize teenage coding rather than detailed parental professions or wealth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen coding, Franceschi cofounder, Brazilian payments gap, YC, second-time founder
evidence_summary: Dubugras and Franceschi built and exited a real payments company (Pagar.me) before finishing college, then used domain insight from that exit plus YC to launch Brex at ~21–22. Primary early stack is deep prior reps with a durable cofounder and structural fintech/startup-credit wave, not inherited capital or family industry. Family finances and parental domain expertise are not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born 1995 in São Paulo, Brazil; self-taught coder from early teens in a Brazilian middle-class tech-interested milieu (family finances not detailed publicly).
current_position: Co-founder and co-CEO of Brex (fintech spend/credit platform); previously recognized among young Brazilian billionaires as Brex scaled; based in the U.S.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Pagar.me, a Brazilian online payments processor, with Pedro Franceschi while still a teenager.
Pagar.me named Microsoft Startup of the Year in the Spark Awards.
Sold Pagar.me to StoneCo for tens of millions after scaling to 100+ employees and ~$1.5B GMV.
Dropped out of Stanford and co-founded Brex (corporate cards for startups) via Y Combinator.
Brex raised large growth rounds and became a widely recognized fintech unicorn serving startups.
Brex valued in the multi-billion range; founders widely covered as young billionaire operators.
Navigated post-SVB banking stress while expanding Brex spend-management products beyond cards.

name: Amir Chetrit
milestone_by_age_26: No verifiable age≤26 milestone. Listed among Ethereum’s early co-founders (joined ~Dec 2013 after Colored Coins / meeting Vitalik), but public sources give no birth year; prior real-estate career through ~2008 implies he was well past 26 by Ethereum’s founding.
early_history_summary: US-Israeli computer-science dropout who worked in real estate before the 2008 crisis, then entered Bitcoin via Colored Coins. Met Vitalik Buterin in 2013 and was among the initial five named Ethereum founders; stepped back mid-2014 after criticism for limited contribution and has since stayed low-profile.
evidence_summary: Without a documented birth year and with a pre-2008 real-estate phase before crypto, there is no independent way to place a material milestone at age ≤26. Ethereum co-founder status (2013–14) is real but undated relative to age.

name: Quincy K. Brown
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 verified. BSEE from NC A&T (1995), MS (2007) and PhD CS (2009) from Drexel, later assistant professor and White House OSTP policy roles; birth year not published and major academic/policy milestones postdate a plausible mid-20s window.
early_history_summary: Graduated Bronx High School of Science; electrical engineering bachelor’s at North Carolina A&T (1995); later returned for graduate CS at Drexel (MS 2007, PhD 2009). Career path includes industry testing roles, Bowie State CS faculty, AnitaB.org leadership, AAAS STEM education work, and OSTP senior policy advisor.
evidence_summary: Brown’s public biography centers on mid-career HCI research, faculty work, and STEM policy leadership. No birth year or independently dated breakout achievement at ≤26 appears in Wikipedia or related profiles reviewed.

name: Nishad Singh
milestone_by_age_26: After graduating UC Berkeley EE summa cum laude (2017) and a brief Facebook engineering stint, joined Alameda Research full-time (Dec 2017, age ~22), became Engineering Manager (~June 2018) then Head of Engineering, and by spring 2019 (~age 24) was Director of Engineering at FTX with a large equity stake—all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born 1995 in the Bay Area (first U.S.-born in family); attended Crystal Springs Uplands School; set a junior ultrarunning world mark (100 miles at 16). Berkeley EE Regents Scholar; graduated 2017; recruited by Sam Bankman-Fried into Alameda/FTX inner engineering circle.
family_context_summary: Born 1995 and raised in the Bay Area; first generation born in the U.S.; father previously received a Berkeley Regents Scholarship path to the U.S. (court sentencing materials).
parent_family_domain_summary: Father’s elite-academic path to the U.S. is noted; not a crypto-industry family business.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Berkeley EE, Bay Area, SBF network, crypto wave, early Alameda/FTX
evidence_summary: Singh combined elite technical training (Berkeley EE, Facebook) with early immersion in the 2017–19 crypto boom via Alameda/FTX leadership roles by age ~23–24. Family provided academic pipeline advantages more than industry capital. Later FTX fraud convictions reframe the legacy but do not erase the dated pre-26 engineering-leadership milestone.
starting_point: Born 1995 in the Bay Area to immigrant parents; first U.S.-born in the family; academically tracked via elite high school and UC Berkeley Regents path.
current_position: Former FTX Director of Engineering; pleaded guilty in the FTX fraud cases and cooperated with prosecutors; sentencing/public status evolved through 2024–25 court process.

trajectory.event: Set a world age-group mark for fastest 100-mile run by a 16-year-old while still in high school.
Graduated UC Berkeley EE summa cum laude; brief software engineering role at Facebook; joined Alameda Research full-time in December.
Promoted to Engineering Manager and then Head of Engineering at Alameda Research.
Became Director of Engineering at FTX while retaining Alameda engineering leadership title and significant equity.
FTX was among the largest crypto exchanges globally with Singh as a core technical executive.
FTX collapsed; Singh left amid the bankruptcy and investigations.
Pleaded guilty to multiple federal fraud-related charges and began cooperating with prosecutors.

name: Andrew Hodges
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. PhD on twistor theory under Roger Penrose awarded 1975 (age ~26) is ordinary doctoral completion; defining fame came with Alan Turing: The Enigma (1983, age ~34).
early_history_summary: Born 1949 in London; PhD Birkbeck (1975) on twistors supervised by Penrose; worked on twistor theory from the early 1970s and was active in gay liberation. Best known later for the definitive Turing biography that inspired Breaking the Code and The Imitation Game.
evidence_summary: Hodges is primarily known as Turing’s biographer (1983) and as a Penrose-lineage twistor mathematician. A 1975 PhD at ~26 is not treated here as a breakout success-by-26 milestone comparable to founding, invention, or major public recognition.

name: Aanand Prasad
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 verified. Candidate appears only as a sparse curated Docker-engineer label; no Wikipedia biography, dated public breakthrough, or reliable birth year found in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Public web footprint insufficient to reconstruct education, employment timeline, or a dated early achievement. Not independently documented as a named Docker core contributor with a public breakout by age 26.
evidence_summary: Insufficient public primary sources to establish identity, birth year, or any independently verifiable ≤26 milestone tied to Docker or other engineering fame.

name: Lachy Groom
category: Stripe early operator / angel investor / robotics founder
milestone_by_age_26: By age ~13–17 sold multiple online businesses (including a PSD-to-WordPress service bought by a U.S. competitor); at ~18 moved to San Francisco and joined Stripe as roughly employee #30 (sources cite ~2012–2014), rising to Head of Issuing—all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born ~1994 in Perth, Western Australia; grandfather taught him HTML/CSS at ~10. Founded PSDtoWP, iPadCaseFinder, supplement and gift-card ventures while at Wesley College; parents Geoff (nuclear physician/radiologist) and Gill supported flexible schooling. Left for Silicon Valley after year 12; Stripe growth/ops/Issuing leadership then full-time angel investing (LGF) and Physical Intelligence co-founding.
family_context_summary: Raised in South Perth; father Geoff is a nuclear physician/radiologist; mother Gill; grandfather taught him web languages—professional middle/upper-middle class Australian household with active parental support of teen entrepreneurship.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father in nuclear medicine/radiology (not software); grandfather provided early HTML/CSS tutoring; no inherited tech-company platform.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen exits, Stripe #30, Perth to SF, online marketplaces, Issuing lead
evidence_summary: Groom’s ≤26 record is unusually dense: multiple teen company sales, early Stripe hire as employee ~#30, and product/ops leadership culminating in Head of Issuing. Family provided stability and early coding exposure rather than Silicon Valley capital; the decisive stack was self-started online businesses plus immersion in Stripe’s growth-stage ecosystem after emigrating at 17–18.
starting_point: Born ~1994 in Perth, Australia, to a professional family (father a nuclear physician); learned web coding from his grandfather and built online businesses through high school.
current_position: Co-founder of robotics/AI company Physical Intelligence; founder of solo GP firm LGF with notable early bets (e.g., Figma, Notion, Ramp); former Head of Stripe Issuing.

trajectory.event: Founded and later sold early web businesses (including PSD-to-WordPress conversion) while still a young teenager.
Featured in The West Australian as an 18-year-old multi-exit internet entrepreneur moving to San Francisco.
Established as early Stripe employee (~#30), working growth, product, and international expansion.
Left Stripe after leading Issuing and related product/ops work to invest full-time.
Raising LGF II (~$100M) as a solo GP after a first fund, with early stakes in later-category-defining SaaS companies.
Raised ~$250M for LGF III, scaling angel/seed strategy.
Co-founded Physical Intelligence, a high-profile robotics foundation-model company in San Francisco.

name: Keith Rabois
milestone_by_age_26: No material tech-operating or founding milestone by age 26 found. Stanford BA (1991, age ~22) and Harvard JD (1994, age ~25) preceded law-firm/clerkship work; PayPal EVP role began ~2000 at age ~31; Square COO, Opendoor, and VC leadership all later.
early_history_summary: Born March 17, 1969; raised in Edison, New Jersey. Political science at Stanford (connected to Peter Thiel/Stanford Review); Harvard Law; appellate clerkship and Sullivan & Cromwell practice; entered tech via PayPal (2000), then LinkedIn, Square COO, Khosla/Founders Fund, and Opendoor co-founding.
family_context_summary: Raised in Edison, New Jersey; detailed parental professions not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Rabois’s defining operating and investing career (PayPal Mafia, Square, Opendoor, major VC platforms) begins in his 30s. Elite degrees by 25 are credentials, not the material independent milestone standard used here for FE eligibility.

name: Annie Easley
milestone_by_age_26: Career began as NACA human computer in 1955 at age 22, but independently dated material technical milestones (Centaur-related programming depth, published NASA technical reports such as 1968/1972 works) are documented later; no specific breakout invention or lead publication by age 26 found—thus treated as age_26_ineligible under strict milestone rule.
early_history_summary: Born April 23, 1933 in Birmingham, Alabama; raised by single mother; valedictorian at Holy Family High School; studied pharmacy at Xavier University of Louisiana before marriage and move to Cleveland. Hired 1955 at NACA Lewis as human computer; 34-year NASA career spanning Fortran/SOAP programming, energy systems, and Centaur support; BS Mathematics Cleveland State (1977); died 2011.
family_context_summary: Born to Bud and Willie (née Sims) McCrory in Birmingham; raised primarily by single mother who strongly pushed education despite Jim Crow segregation.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother emphasized education; no documented STEM professional pipeline in the family.
evidence_summary: Easley is a major NASA computing pioneer, but the strict ≤26 rule requires a dated material breakout, not only early employment. Documented technical publications and Centaur-era recognition concentrate after her mid-20s; eligibility denied conservatively.

name: David Schwartz
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. Early private firm (David Schwartz Enterprise ~1988) and EE degree (~1990) are not documented breakouts; joined Ripple ~2011 as chief cryptographer (age ~41–42) and later CTO—fame is mid-career crypto infrastructure.
early_history_summary: U.S. cryptographer often cited as born 1969 (sometimes listed ~1970); studied electrical engineering (University of Houston ~1990 per secondary sources). Pre-Ripple career includes early entrepreneurial and cryptography/software work; original XRP Ledger architect after joining Ripple in 2011; later CTO and CTO Emeritus.
evidence_summary: Schwartz’s independently notable achievement is architecting and leading technology at Ripple/XRP Ledger beginning around age 41–42. Pre-26 activity lacks two-source dated material milestones suitable for eligibility.

name: Aaron Iba
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded AppJet (YC, 2007) at age ~24; launched Etherpad (first widely noted web realtime collaborative editor, 2008–2009) and sold AppJet/Etherpad to Google in December 2009 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born June 18, 1983; grew up in Lexington, Massachusetts; MIT mathematics degree (2005). With David Greenspan won MIT Battlecode (2003); founded AppJet in YC, pivoted tools into Etherpad, then joined Google post-acquisition; later YC partner (2011–2013) and PayGarden founder.
family_context_summary: Raised in Lexington, Massachusetts; detailed parental professions not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT, Battlecode, YC, Greenspan cofounder, Etherpad, Google acquisition
evidence_summary: Iba’s path is classic elite-pipeline + technical depth: MIT, competition-winning partnership with Greenspan, YC-backed AppJet, and a category-defining collab product (Etherpad) acquired by Google by age 26. Family background is sparsely documented; institutional and peer advantages dominate the early stack.
starting_point: Born 1983 and raised in Lexington, Massachusetts; attended MIT (math, class of 2005).
current_position: Entrepreneur and angel investor; former YC partner; founded PayGarden after leaving YC; associated with later ventures including Lightweight Labs.

trajectory.event: With David Greenspan, won MIT’s Battlecode programming competition.
Graduated MIT with a mathematics degree.
Co-founded AppJet through Y Combinator, building JavaScript hosting/dev tools.
Launched Etherpad, a pioneering real-time collaborative web text editor built with AppJet tech.
Google acquired AppJet/Etherpad; team and tech merged toward Google Wave efforts.
Became a full-time Y Combinator partner, investing and advising startups.
Left YC to found PayGarden, an alternative payments company for unused gift cards.
